items.text: 2025 marked the 50th anniversary of digital photography.
Steve Sasson, inventor of the first digital camera in 1975, told the BBC that it looked like a 'toaster with a lens' - not like the stylish cameras we see today!

level1.text: inventor of the first digital camera in 1975

items.text: By 2005, more people were buying digital cameras than film cameras, which meant that a process which used to be slow and laborious, was now quick and easy.

level2.label: 宾语从句

items.text: The 2000s brought a snap-happy era, with people now able to take hundreds, even thousands of photos a year.
But what they hadn't quite worked out yet was how to store them.

level1.label: 主语从句
level1.text: what they hadn't quite worked out yet

items.text: Back then, people used a mishmash of hard drives, USB sticks and CDs - physical storage that was at risk of loss or theft.

level1.label: 同位语

level2.label: 定语从句

items.text: Later came online photo sharing via social media or free online photo galleries where you can upload photos to 'the cloud'.

level2.label: 定语从句

items.text: The problem is that if you chose just one of these options for photo storage, such as an old laptop that's now broken, or a social media website that no longer exists, you may have what's called a 'black hole' in your photographic record, with no photos of life in the noughties.

level1.label: 表语从句

items.text: After losing an external hard drive with all her family photos, Cathi Nelson set up The Photo Managers, a company which helps people manage their photo collections.

level2.label: 定语从句

items.text: They say the best protection is their '3-2-1' rule of photo storage which involves having three copies of each photo, all in different places.

items.text: One in the cloud, the second on a hard drive, and a third on a drive in a separate location, like someone else's house.
If that sounds like too much work, just make sure your smartphone automatically uploads photos to the cloud, and then spare some time once a month to upload those to a hard drive.

items.text: And if you're someone who takes hundreds of photos per month, it's also a good idea to regularly curate your camera roll - keep the best ones and delete the rest, so you feel more in control.

items.text: The key takeaway here is that each storage method has its pitfalls, so it's better to always use two methods over just one in order to have a backup.

Just make sure your memories don't fade into the digital black hole.
